heightEncoding.note: The grid is authoritative for walkability. The Godot loader takes elevation from the rendered walk surfaces, not from this file.

notes: Every terrain sub-mesh is named Terrain_<class>; every authored walkable deck is named Walk_<name>. Structural geometry is deliberately not a walk surface, so the grounding ray never snaps an actor onto a roof, a gantry or the top of an arch.

landmarks.name: The Snowline Stones
landmarks.note: Ten cut stones up the slope, each with a brass line where the snow stood the year it was set. The last three stand above the snow now.

landmarks.name: The Mirrorhold March
landmarks.note: Where the Whitehorn Range gives way to Mirrorhold: votary road furniture, a march stone, a waystation, and 10 pieces of the country beyond.

landmarks.name: The Amber Pass
landmarks.note: Where the Whitehorn Range gives way to the Amberwood: votary road furniture, a march stone, a waystation, and 10 pieces of the country beyond.

landmarks.name: The Barrens Pass
landmarks.note: Where the Whitehorn Range gives way to the Amethyst Barrens: votary road furniture, a march stone, a waystation, and 12 pieces of the country beyond.

notes: Whitehorn has no sea and no standing water; the watercourses are frozen or dry meltwater beds.
sun.direction is the direction the light travels, so its Y is negative. See _environment() in source/build_whitehorn.py.

transform.formula: pixel_x = world_x * scale + offset; pixel_y = world_z * scale + offset

minimap.note: Every Eloria minimap is drawn at one pixel to the metre, so the image's pixel size is the map's size in metres.

provenance.assets: All geometry and textures generated procedurally; no third-party models or images.
